item.title: Canada Pushes Back as US Trade Talks Collapse
item.description: Bloomberg News Executive Editor for Canada Derek Decloet joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains that Canadians are frustrated but not necessarily surprised after last-minute US-Canada negotiations collapsed, triggering 50% US tariffs on about $20 billion of Canadian goods and a dollar-for-dollar retaliation pledge from Ottawa. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia’s Rosatom Returns Workers to Iran’s Bushehr Nuclear Plant
item.description: Russia state-owned atomic energy company Rosatom is continuing to return employees to Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant, Interfax reported, citing the company’s Chief Executive Officer Alexey Likhachev.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Bond Market Tests Limits of Treasury Intervention
item.description: Joining Bloomberg This Weekend is Bloomberg Radio host of "Masters in Business" Barry Ritholtz and he tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s bond-market moves may provide short-term relief but cannot override persistent inflation, rising debt and the forces setting long-term yields. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: BTW: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: LinkedIn becoming a dating site, ghost jobs, fun at home, and farmers saying no to data centers: Alexis Christoforous joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to share headlines from this week that may have gone under the radar. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Chinese AI Models Gain Ground on Price and Use
item.description: Chinese AI models are rapidly narrowing the performance gap with US rivals while gaining users with lower prices and open-weight technology that lets companies deploy them locally. Bloomberg News Tech Reporter Luz Ding is on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains to hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Chinese AI Models capabilities are approaching leading US models at lower cost. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Supreme Court Keeps Trump Ballroom Work Going
item.description: Chief Justice John Roberts temporarily allowed construction of President Donald Trump’s White House ballroom to continue while the Supreme Court considers whether to grant a longer stay, after lower courts said the project required congressional authorization. Bloomberg News Supreme Court Reporter Greg Stohr joins hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to explain that the court also weighs challenges involving Trump’s mail ballot order and the administration prepares for expected litigation over its new Canada tariffs. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The AI Spending Spree Comes With a Catch
item.description: Sam Palmisano says the AI boom is built on long-cycle bets in data centers, chips and energy, even as AI software changes at breakneck speed. If adoption slows or cheaper Chinese open-source models gain traction, Big Tech may have to rethink the spending plans behind today’s AI race. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Investing in AI for More Jobs, Less Pay
item.description: The good news and bad news about AI
item.dc:creator: David Westin

item.title: India’s Foreign Minister to Visit Russia Amid US Tariff Threat
item.description: India‘s External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar will visit Russia and co-chair the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission meeting on trade, science, technology, and culture.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Mishra

item.title: India’s Central Bank Says Forex Deposit Inflows at $65.4 Billion
item.description: India garnered over $65 billion through special foreign currency deposits from its 35 million-strong diaspora, latest figures from the central bank showed Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Mishra

item.title: Mexico Optimistic it Can Achieve Lower US Tariffs on Cars, Steel
item.description: Mexico’s top trade negotiator expressed optimism he can secure less burdensome tariff terms from the US on Mexican automobile and steel exports, similar to revised measures Washington is discussing with Canada.
item.dc:creator: Alex Vasquez

item.title: Wall Street Week | AI Hits Wages, USMCA Under Pressure, Colorado River Crisis
item.description: This week, Former IBM CEO Sam Palmisano discusses why companies may benefit from having a “Plan B” for AI implementation. And, AI may not be causing mass layoffs yet, but early data suggest it is already slowing wage growth in exposed occupations. Plus, Canada may have dodged Trump’s newest tariffs, but the deal could leave lasting damage to USMCA, North American manufacturing and trust between two longtime allies. Later, who pays when the Colorado River can no longer meet the West’s demand? (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lula Holds Lead Over Bolsonaro Six Weeks From Brazilian Election
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva maintained his lead over right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of Brazil’s October election, a new poll found.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Diniz Tavares

item.title: Moderna, Merck Cancer Vax Gives Hope
item.description: Scientists are on the cusp of fulfilling a decades-long quest: to use vaccines to teach the immune system to spot and destroy cancer cells. News that an mRNA cancer vaccine developed by Merck & Co. and Moderna Inc. kept melanoma from returning in a large, late-stage trial marks a critical next chapter for a technology beleaguered by post-pandemic political backlash and years of false starts before then. Bloomberg Opinion Columnist Lisa Jarvis writes "Moderna and Merck's Cancer Vaccine Is a Marvel." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Allows Tariff Relief for Some Ground Beef Imports
item.description: President Donald Trump is aiming to deliver cost relief for some ground beef imports to lower prices for American consumers, by allowing up to 300,000 metric tons of product for ground beef to be imported with no out of quota tariff for the next 90 days. He also made a commitment that the beef will be sold at 25% below current market prices. Agriculture Reporter Ilena Peng and Howard Capital Management CEO Vance Howard -- who owns a ranch of his own -- discuss how much the tariff relief will impact costs, and what it may do to American farm businesses. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Young People Don't Believe in 'American Dream': Kevin Gordon
item.description: Kevin Gordon, head of macro research & strategy at Schwab Center for Financial Research, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Jerry Maguire’ Inspiration on Lakers, Sports Valuations
item.description: Leigh Steinberg, legendary sports agent and founder of the Leigh Steinberg Foundation, spoke about the unprecedented valuations in the sports industry, highlighting the ongoing Los Angeles Lakers sale currently valued at $12.5 billion. He emphasized the dramatic increase in franchise values over the decades, noting that when he started in 1976, NFL expansion teams were purchased for $16.5 million, compared to recent sales reaching into the billions. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Parents Spend $95K on Gap Years to Give Their Kids an Edge
item.description: Bloomberg's Sarah Foster joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." Gap years are becoming more appealing as families question whether a college degree alone is enough to stand out, with some programs costing more than a year of tuition. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mexico Governor Accused by US of Cartel Ties Returns to Post
item.description: The Mexican governor accused by the US of conspiring with a major criminal cartel to traffic drugs is ending his leave of absence, pledging to finish out his term through next year in a move that could inflame tensions with Washington.
item.dc:creator: Gonzalo Soto and Alex Vasquez

item.title: Vingroup Among Vietnam Stocks to Debut on FTSE’s EM Index
item.description: Vingroup JSC is among over 100 Vietnamese companies added to FTSE Russell’s Global Equity Indexes late Friday, marking a key step in the country’s long-awaited transition from frontier to secondary emerging market status.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen Kieu Giang
